result.title: Neural Rendering Compiler: Generative Video Models as Programmable Renderers
result.summary: Generative video models are becoming powerful renderers, yet lack the predictable control interfaces of conventional systems such as HTML/CSS engines or Blender. Their capabilities emerge implicitly from training, making it difficult to determine what they can reliably execute. We present Neural Rendering Compiler (NeurCo), which automatically probes frozen video models to construct model-specific capability manuals describing which semantic requirements they can reliably satisfy. NeurCo represents user intent in a model-agnostic intermediate representation of objects, constraints, events, and cameras, then compiles it into model-specific execution strategies. Reliable requirements remain unchanged, while unreliable ones are selectively rewritten or compiled into alternative execution strategies. We introduce VComBench, a benchmark of 380 compositional, multi-requirement tasks spanning text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-to-video generation. NeurCo improves requirement satisfaction from 46.8% to 52.3% on Wan and from 66.5% to 69.3% on Minimax H3, and achieves further gains when combined with prompt enhancers, including on Seedance 2.5. Our analysis reveals model-specific differences in control capabilities and trade-offs between controllability and photorealism, highlighting capability-guided compilation as a promising approach to programmable generative video rendering.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 NeurCo，把用户意图表示为对象、约束、事件、相机的模型无关中间表示，通过探测冻结视频模型构建「能力手册」，并编译为模型特定的执行策略，同时发布 380 项组合任务的 VComBench。
AI.relevance_reason: 「探测冻结模型可靠能力边界，再对不可靠需求改写或换用替代执行策略」的思路可能可供核查，对应 LVR 中判断哪些视觉证据需求可被可靠满足以及动态计算与回退设计；但该工作面向视频渲染生成，与 latent 推理状态表示无直接联系。
